page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3.26xlarge is a storage-optimized instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 104 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 architecture, utilizing Intel Xeon 8269CY processors running at 2.5 GHz. With a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio, each of the 104 vCPUs maps to a dedicated physical core, ensuring consistent compute performance without hyperthreading resource contention.

The instance is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 7.38 GB of RAM per core. A key hardware feature is the integrated local storage, consisting of 23038 GB of SSD capacity. This massive local storage volume is bundled directly with the instance, making it suitable for high-throughput, low-latency I/O operations. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 32 Gbps.

Given the combination of high-capacity local SSD storage, substantial memory, and dedicated Intel Xeon cores, the ecs.i3.26xlarge is designed for resource-intensive workloads. It is highly suited for large-scale relational and non-relational databases, data warehousing, and big data analytics engines that require rapid access to local storage. The dedicated core allocation offers predictable compute performance, though the lack of GPU acceleration limits its applicability for heavy deep learning training workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3.26xlarge is a high-capacity, storage-optimized server designed for demanding database and data-processing workloads. Powered by the KVM hypervisor, it features 104 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 architecture using Intel Xeon 8269CY processors clocked at 2.5 GHz. The instance provides 768.0 GB of RAM, translating to 7.38 GB per core, and includes a massive 23038 GB of local SSD storage. With a baseline network bandwidth of 32 Gbps and a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio, it delivers highly predictable compute and I/O performance. This hardware profile is optimized for large-scale databases, data warehousing, and big data analytics where massive local storage and high memory capacity are critical. It does not include GPU accelerators, making it a dedicated choice for storage-heavy and memory-intensive CPU workloads.
